newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Pipeline says not threatened by pullout.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Pipeline says not threatened by pullout.

text.p: Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd's decision to pull out of a consortium planning an Alberta natural gas pipeline does not threaten the project's viability, a consortium official said on Thursday.

Proponents of the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day Alberta Pipeline Project (APP) proposal said earlier Amoco was selling its stake to partners ATCO Ltd unit ATCO Gas Pipelines and Shell Canada Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
"They've only decided not to be an equity participant. It wasn't a core investment for them," ATCO Gas Pipelines vice-president Russ Kupin said.
Kupin said Amoco was still planning to be a major shipper on the line, which would be in service in 1999.
Besides Shell and Amoco, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada was also pledging gas volumes on the APP, a line that would compete with NOVA Corp in Alberta.
NOVA Gas Transmission's network currently moves virtually all of the gas produced in Alberta, an amount equal to about 18 percent of North America's supply.
APP said it planned to apply for Canadian National Energy Board approval July after an open season to gauge support from other shippers slated for May.
Pipeline construction was planned for the spring and summer of 1999, with completion set for November 1999 to coincide with planned expansions of downstream pipeline capacity, the firms said.

Kupin said APP was not designed to meet the same fate as the Palliser Pipeline, the PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd -led project that would have shipped about 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas to the Alberta-Saskatchewan border from north of Calgary in competition with NOVA.

NOVA and PanCanadian struck a deal in December to give the producer and its supporters a cheaper "load-retention" transport rate on the NGTL network, which effectively killed the project and raised questions in some industry circles about whether Palliser had become a bargaining chip for preferred NOVA tolls.
"That's not our intention at all," said Kupin, whose firm owns two gas utilities in Alberta.
He said the main motivation for the project was to allow the shippers' production to flow to planned increased export pipeline capacity at competitive tolling rates.
Kupin said, however, that questions regarding comparisons to Palliser were the most common asked of APP officials.
